questions.text:
मगध के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से विकल्प सही हैं?
I. मगध एक बहुत शक्तिशाली महाजनपद था।
II. राजगाह मगध की राजधानी थी।
III. मगध अर्ध-शुष्क क्षेत्र में था।
IV. मगध प्राकृतिक संसाधनों से समृद्ध था।
विकल्प:
(A) I, II और IV सही हैं
(B) I, II और III सही हैं
(C) I, III और IV सही हैं
(D) II, III और IV सही हैं
questions.text_english:
Which of the following options are correct regarding Magadha?
I. Magadha was the most powerful Mahajanapada.
II. Rajgaha was the capital of Magadha.
III. Magadha was in a semi-arid area.
IV. Magadha was rich in natural resources.
Options:
(A) I, II and IV are correct
(B) I, II and III are correct
(C) I, III and IV are correct
(D) II, III and IV are correct

options.A: I, II और IV सही हैं
options.B: I, II और III सही हैं
options.C: I, III और IV सही हैं
options.D: II, III और IV सही हैं

options_english.A: I, II and IV are correct
options_english.B: I, II and III are correct
options_english.C: I, III and IV are correct
options_english.D: II, III and IV are correct

questions.solution: Magadha became the most powerful Mahajanapada due to its strategic location, availability of natural resources like iron mines, and fertile land. Its first capital was Rajgaha (present-day Rajgir). Therefore, statements I, II, and IV are correct, while statement III is incorrect as it was not in a semi-arid area.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित को कालानुक्रम से क्रमबद्ध कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
I. अशोक का शासन
II. महापद्मनंद का शासन
III. हर्षवर्धन का शासन
IV. समुद्रगुप्त का शासन
विकल्प:
(A) I, III, IV, II
(B) III, II, I, IV
(C) II, I, IV, III
(D) IV, III, I, II
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following in chronological order and choose the correct option:
I. Rule of Asoka
II. Rule of Mahapadma Nanda
III. Rule of Harshavardhana
IV. Rule of Samudragupta
Options:
(A) I, III, IV, II
(B) III, II, I, IV
(C) II, I, IV, III
(D) IV, III, I, II
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is Mahapadma Nanda (c. 4th century BCE), followed by Asoka (c. 3rd century BCE), then Samudragupta (c. 4th century CE), and finally Harshavardhana (c. 7th century CE). Thus, the sequence is II, I, IV, III.

questions.text:
स्तम्भ I का मिलान स्तम्भ II से कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
स्तम्भ I (महाभारत के पात्र) - स्तम्भ II (भूमिका)
1. दुर्योधन - (i) हिडिम्बा का पुत्र
2. गांधारी - (ii) धृतराष्ट्र का ज्येष्ठ पुत्र
3. कुंती - (iii) पांडवों की माता
4. घटोत्कच - (iv) दुर्योधन की माता
विकल्प: (A) 1-(iv), 2-(iii), 3-(ii), 4-(i) (B) 1-(ii), 2-(i), 3-(iv), 4-(iii) (C) 1-(ii), 2-(i), 3-(iii), 4-(iv) (D) 1-(ii), 2-(iv), 3-(iii), 4-(i)
questions.text_english:
Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option:
Column I (Characters of Mahabharata) - Column II (Role)
1. Duryodhana - (i) Son of Hidimba
2. Gandhari - (ii) Eldest son of Dhritrashtra
3. Kunti - (iii) Mother of Pandavas
4. Ghatotkacha - (iv) Mother of Duryodhana
Options: (A) 1-(iv), 2-(iii), 3-(ii), 4-(i) (B) 1-(ii), 2-(i), 3-(iv), 4-(iii) (C) 1-(ii), 2-(i), 3-(iii), 4-(iv) (D) 1-(ii), 2-(iv), 3-(iii), 4-(i)
questions.solution: Matching the characters correctly: Duryodhana was the eldest son of Dhritrashtra (1-ii), Gandhari was the mother of Duryodhana (2-iv), Kunti was the mother of Pandavas (3-iii), and Ghatotkacha was the son of Hidimba (4-i). Option (D) correctly represents this matching.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से किस कला शैली को बुद्ध की दी गई मूर्तिकला छवि में दर्शाया गया है?
(A) अमरावती कला शैली
(B) मथुरा कला शैली
(C) गांधार कला शैली
(D) गॉथिक कला शैली
questions.text_english:
Which of the following schools of art is depicted in the given sculpture image of Buddha?
(A) Amravati school of art
(B) Mathura school of art
(C) Gandhara school of art
(D) Gothic school of art
questions.solution: The sculpture of Buddha shown is characteristic of the Mathura school of art, which is known for its distinctive facial features and style of carving the Buddha's robes compared to the Gandhara style.

questions.text:
_______ का हड़प्पा पुरास्थल वर्तमान राजस्थान में स्थित है।
(A) राखीगढ़ी
(B) लोथल
(C) कालीबंगन
(D) मांडा
questions.text_english:
The Harappan site of _______ is located in present day Rajasthan.
(A) Rakhigarhi
(B) Lothal
(C) Kalibangan
(D) Manda
questions.solution: Kalibangan is a major Harappan site located in the Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan, India. Other options like Lothal (Gujarat) and Rakhigarhi (Haryana) are located elsewhere.

questions.text:
कनिंघम के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों को पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
I. कनिंघम भारतीय पुरातात्त्विक सर्वेक्षण का पहला डायरेक्टर-जनरल था।
II. उसने 19वीं शताब्दी के मध्य में पुरातात्त्विक उत्खनन का कार्य आरम्भ किया।
III. उसने पुरातत्त्व की पद्धति में सैनिक परिशुद्धता का समावेश किया।
IV. उसने चीनी बौद्ध तीर्थयात्रियों द्वारा छोड़े गए वृत्तांतों का प्रयोग किया।
विकल्प:
(A) I और IV सही हैं
(B) I और II सही हैं
(C) I, II और III सही हैं
(D) I, II और IV सही हैं
questions.text_english:
Read the following statements regarding Cunningham and choose the correct option:
I. Cunningham was the first Director-General of ASI.
II. He began archaeological excavations in mid 19th century.
III. He brought a military precision to the practice of archaeology.
IV. He used the accounts left by Chinese Buddhist pilgrims.
Options:
(A) I and IV are correct
(B) I and II are correct
(C) I, II and III are correct
(D) I, II and IV are correct

options.C: I, II और III सही हैं
options.D: I, II और IV सही हैं

options_english.C: I, II and III are correct
options_english.D: I, II and IV are correct

questions.solution: Alexander Cunningham was the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). He initiated excavations in the mid-19th century, used accounts of Chinese Buddhist pilgrims, and had a military background. Statements I, II, and IV are the most accurate summary of his major contributions as noted in the curriculum.

questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं, अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R)।
अभिकथन (A): इब्न बतूता ने भारतीय कृषि को बहुत उत्पादक पाया।
कारण (R): मिट्टी उपजाऊ थी जिससे किसानों को साल में दो फसलों को उगाना संभव था।
विकल्प: (A) A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या करता है। (B) A और R दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। (C) A सही है, परन्तु R ग़लत है। (D) A ग़लत है, परन्तु R सही है।
questions.text_english:
Two statements as Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below.
Assertion (A): Ibn Battuta found Indian agriculture very productive.
Reason (R): The soils were fertile which allowed the farmers to produce two crops a year.
Options: (A) Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A. (B) Both A and R are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A. (C) A is correct, but R is incorrect. (D) A is incorrect, but R is correct.

options.A: A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: A और R दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: A सही है, परन्तु R ग़लत है।
options.D: A ग़लत है, परन्तु R सही है।

options_english.A: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is correct, but R is incorrect.
options_english.D: A is incorrect, but R is correct.

questions.solution: Ibn Battuta, the traveler, specifically noted the high productivity of Indian agriculture during his visit, attributing it to the fertile soil that allowed for multiple cropping in a year. The reason (R) provides the direct explanation for the assertion (A).

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित जानकारी की सहायता से व्यक्ति की पहचान कीजिए:
वह एक प्रसिद्ध अभियंता, सर्वेक्षक और मानचित्रकार था। 1815 में उसे भारत का पहला सर्वेयर जनरल बनाया गया।
(A) अलेक्जेंडर ग्रीनलॉ
(B) कॉलिन मैकेंज़ी
(C) जॉन मार्शल
(D) आर.ई.एम. व्हीलर
questions.text_english:
Identify the person with the help of following information:
He was a famous engineer, surveyor and cartographer. He was appointed the first Surveyor General of India in 1815.
(A) Alexander Greenlaw
(B) Colin Mackenzie
(C) John Marshall
(D) R.E.M. Wheeler
questions.solution: Colin Mackenzie was an engineer, surveyor, and cartographer who became the first Surveyor General of India in 1815. He is well-known for his extensive documentation of Indian historical sites.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा जोड़ा सही सुमेलित है?
(A) चिदम्बरम मंदिर - तंजावुर
(B) बृहदेश्वर मंदिर - विजयनगर
(C) चन्नकेश्व मंदिर - बेलूर
(D) हज़ार राम मंदिर - तमिलनाडु
questions.text_english:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
(A) Chidambaram Temple - Thanjavur
(B) Brihadishvara Temple - Vijayanagara
(C) Chennakeshava Temple - Belur
(D) Hazara Rama Temple - Tamil Nadu
questions.solution: The Chennakeshava Temple is indeed located at Belur. The Brihadishvara Temple is in Thanjavur, and Hazara Rama Temple is in the ruins of Vijayanagara city, making other options incorrect.

questions.text:
मुगल काल में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कबीला भारत और अफ़ग़ानिस्तान के बीच ज़मीनी व्यापार में लगा था और पंजाब के गाँवों और शहरों में भी शिरकत करता था?
(A) मुंडा
(B) कोच
(C) अहोम
(D) लोहानी
questions.text_english:
Which one of the following tribes was engaged in overland trade between India and Afghanistan and in the villages and towns in Punjab during the Mughal era?
(A) Mundas
(B) Koch
(C) Ahoms
(D) Lohanis
questions.solution: The Lohani tribe was known during the Mughal period for engaging in the overland trade between India and Afghanistan and participating in trade within the villages and towns of Punjab.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा जोड़ा सही सुमेलित है?
(A) कबीरदास - कर्नाटक
(B) मीराबाई - राजस्थान
(C) बासवन्ना - असम
(D) शंकरदेव - उत्तर प्रदेश
questions.text_english:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
(A) Kabirdas - Karnataka
(B) Mirabai - Rajasthan
(C) Basavanna - Assam
(D) Shankaradeva - Uttar Pradesh
questions.solution: Mirabai was a prominent saint-poet from Rajasthan. The other options are incorrect: Kabir was from UP, Basavanna was from Karnataka, and Shankaradeva was from Assam.

questions.text:
स्तम्भ I का मिलान स्तम्भ II से कीजिए:
स्तम्भ I (1857 के विद्रोह के नेता) - स्तम्भ II (संबंधित क्षेत्र)
1. कुँवर सिंह - (i) सिंहभूम
2. शाह मल - (ii) आरा
3. बिरजिस क़द्र - (iii) बड़ौत
4. गोनू - (iv) लखनऊ
विकल्प: (A) 1-(i), 2-(ii), 3-(iii), 4-(iv) (B) 1-(iii), 2-(ii), 3-(iv), 4-(i) (C) 1-(ii), 2-(iii), 3-(iv), 4-(i) (D) 1-(iv), 2-(ii), 3-(iii), 4-(i)
questions.text_english:
Match Column I with Column II:
Column I (Leaders of the Revolt of 1857) - Column II (Related Region)
1. Kunwar Singh - (i) Singhbhum
2. Shah Mal - (ii) Arrah
3. Birjis Qadr - (iii) Barout
4. Gonoo - (iv) Lucknow
Options: (A) 1-(i), 2-(ii), 3-(iii), 4-(iv) (B) 1-(iii), 2-(ii), 3-(iv), 4-(i) (C) 1-(ii), 2-(iii), 3-(iv), 4-(i) (D) 1-(iv), 2-(ii), 3-(iii), 4-(i)
questions.solution: Kunwar Singh led in Arrah (1-ii), Shah Mal led in Barout (2-iii), Birjis Qadr in Lucknow (3-iv), and Gonoo in Singhbhum (4-i). Option (C) matches these.
questions.chapter: Colonialism and the Countryside / Rebels and the Raj

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से किसने महाभारत का समालोचनात्मक संस्करण तैयार करने का ज़िम्मा उठाया?
(A) डी.एन. झा
(B) इरावती कार्वे
(C) वी.एस. सुकथांकर
(D) राम करण शर्मा
questions.text_english:
Who among the following initiated the task of preparing the critical edition of Mahabharata?
(A) D.N. Jha
(B) Irawati Karve
(C) V.S. Sukthankar
(D) Ram Karan Sharma
questions.solution: V.S. Sukthankar was the lead scholar who initiated and directed the ambitious project of creating a critical edition of the Mahabharata, which involved comparing manuscripts from across the subcontinent.

questions.text:
स्तम्भ I का मिलान स्तम्भ II से कीजिए:
स्तम्भ I (यात्री) - स्तम्भ II (लिखी गई किताबें)
1. अबुल फज़ल - (i) ट्रैवल्स इन द मुगल एम्पायर
2. इब्न बतूता - (ii) किताब-उल-हिन्द
3. अल-बिरुनी - (iii) रिहला
4. फ्राँस्वा बर्नियर - (iv) आइन-ए-अकबरी
विकल्प: (A) 1-(iv), 2-(iii), 3-(ii), 4-(i) (B) 1-(iii), 2-(ii), 3-(i), 4-(iv) (C) 1-(ii), 2-(i), 3-(iv), 4-(iii) (D) 1-(i), 2-(iii), 3-(ii), 4-(iv)
questions.text_english:
Match Column I with Column II:
Column I (Traveller) - Column II (Books authored)
1. Abu'l Fazl - (i) Travels in the Mughal Empire
2. Ibn Battuta - (ii) Kitab-ul-Hind
3. Al-Biruni - (iii) Rihla
4. François Bernier - (iv) Ain-i-Akbari
Options: (A) 1-(iv), 2-(iii), 3-(ii), 4-(i) (B) 1-(iii), 2-(ii), 3-(i), 4-(iv) (C) 1-(ii), 2-(i), 3-(iv), 4-(iii) (D) 1-(i), 2-(iii), 3-(ii), 4-(iv)
questions.solution: Abu'l Fazl wrote Ain-i-Akbari (1-iv), Ibn Battuta wrote Rihla (2-iii), Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind (3-ii), and François Bernier wrote Travels in the Mughal Empire (4-i). Option (A) is correct.

questions.text:
मुगल साम्राज्य की वह ज़मीन जिसमें एक के बाद एक फ़सल की सालाना खेती होती थी, को _______ कहा जाता था।
(A) पोलज
(B) परौती
(C) बंजर
(D) चचर
questions.text_english:
The land which was annually cultivated for each crop in succession was called _______ in the Mughal Empire.
(A) Polaj
(B) Parauti
(C) Banjar
(D) Chachar
questions.solution: In the Mughal land revenue system, 'Polaj' was the term used for land that was under constant cultivation, allowing for annual cropping for every crop in succession.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से किस जिले में रैयतों ने रैयतवाड़ी व्यवस्था में साहूकारों के विरुद्ध विद्रोह किया था?
(A) अवध
(B) बैरकपुर
(C) भागलपुर
(D) पूना
questions.text_english:
In which of the following districts did the ryots revolt against sahukars of the Ryotwari system?
(A) Awadh
(B) Barrackpore
(C) Bhagalpur
(D) Poona
questions.solution: The Deccan Riots of 1875 occurred in the Poona district, where peasants revolted against the moneylenders (sahukars) due to their exploitative practices under the British land revenue systems.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन भारतीय राष्ट्रीय काँग्रेस के नरम दल से संबंधित थे?
(A) बिपिन चंद्र पाल
(B) बाल गंगाधर तिलक
(C) गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले
(D) लाला लाजपत राय
questions.text_english:
Who among the following belonged to a Moderate group of Indian National Congress?
(A) Bipin Chandra Pal
(B) Bal Gangadhar Tilak
(C) Gopal Krishan Gokhale
(D) Lala Lajpat Rai
questions.solution: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a prominent leader of the Moderate faction of the Indian National Congress. The others (Pal, Tilak, and Rai) belonged to the Extremist faction.
questions.chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

questions.text:
'भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन' से संबंधित निम्नलिखित कथनों में से कौन-सा सही नहीं है?
(A) भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन एक जन आंदोलन था।
(B) हजारों भारतीयों ने इस आंदोलन में भाग लिया।
(C) सतारा और मेदिनीपुर में 'स्वतंत्र' सरकार की स्थापना कर दी गई।
(D) रजवाड़ों में 'प्रजा मंडलों' की एक श्रृंखला स्थापित की गई।
questions.text_english:
Which of the following statements is not correct regarding 'Quit India Movement'?
(A) Quit India Movement was a mass movement.
(B) Thousands of Indians took part in this movement.
(C) 'Independent' governments were proclaimed in Satara and Medinipur.
(D) A series of 'Praja Mandals' were established in princely states.

options.A: भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन एक जन आंदोलन था।
options.B: हजारों भारतीयों ने इस आंदोलन में भाग लिया।
options.C: सतारा और मेदिनीपुर में 'स्वतंत्र' सरकार की स्थापना कर दी गई।
options.D: रजवाड़ों में 'प्रजा मंडलों' की एक श्रृंखला स्थापित की गई।

options_english.A: Quit India Movement was a mass movement.
options_english.B: Thousands of Indians took part in this movement.
options_english.C: 'Independent' governments were proclaimed in Satara and Medinipur.
options_english.D: A series of 'Praja Mandals' were established in princely states.

questions.solution: Options A, B, and C are correct descriptions of the Quit India Movement. Option D is incorrect because Praja Mandals were established long before the Quit India movement as part of the struggle for democratic rights in princely states, not as a specific feature of this movement.
questions.chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

questions.text:
खूब लड़ी मर्दानी, वह तो झाँसी वाली रानी थी।

questions.text_english:
Khoob ladi mardani, woh to Jhansi wali rani thi.
Who among the following has written these lines and portrayed Laxmi Bai as a symbol to resist injustice?
(A) Sarojini Naidu
(B) Suryakant Tripathi Nirala
(C) Harivansh Rai Bachchan
(D) Subhadra Kumari Chauhan
questions.solution: These famous lines are from the poem 'Jhansi ki Rani' written by the renowned poet Subhadra Kumari Chauhan, who celebrated Rani Laxmi Bai's bravery and resistance against British colonial rule.

questions.text_english:
Who among the following introduced the 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly on 13th December, 1946?
(A) Vallabh Bhai Patel
(B) B.R. Ambedkar
(C) Jawaharlal Nehru
(D) Rajendra Prasad
questions.solution: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly on December 13, 1946, outlining the guiding principles for the framing of the Indian Constitution.

questions.text:
संविधान सभा में केन्द्र में मजबूत सरकार बनाने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से किस पर चर्चा की गई? सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
I. देश के कल्याण के लिए योजना बनाने के लिए।
II. राज्य स्तर पर मजबूत प्रशासन स्थापित करने के लिए।
III. उपलब्ध आर्थिक संसाधनों को जुटाने के लिए।
IV. विदेशी आक्रमण से देश की रक्षा करने के लिए।
विकल्प:
(A) I, II और IV
(B) I, II और III
(C) II, III और IV
(D) I, III और IV
questions.text_english:
Which of the following were discussed in the Constituent Assembly for making a strong government at the Centre? Choose the correct option from the following:
I. Planning for the well-being of the country.
II. To establish strong administration at the state level.
III. To mobilise available economic resources.
IV. To defend the country against foreign aggression.
Options:
(A) I, II and IV
(B) I, II and III
(C) II, III and IV
(D) I, III and IV
questions.solution: The debate for a strong Centre revolved around the need for planning (I), mobilization of resources (III), and national defense (IV). Establishing a strong administration at the state level (II) was generally contrasted with the push for a strong Centre.

(क) विभिन्न स्थलों पर हड़प्पावासियों द्वारा उपयोग की जाने वाली सिंचाई की विधियों की व्याख्या कीजिए।

(ख) हड़प्पा सभ्यता में लोगों के बीच सामाजिक और आर्थिक अंतरों को समझने में शवाधान किस प्रकार सहायक हैं, व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Explain the methods of irrigation used by the Harappans at different sites.
OR
(b) Explain how burials help in understanding the social and economic differences amongst the people in Harappan civilization.

sub_questions.text: हड़प्पावासियों द्वारा उपयोग की जाने वाली सिंचाई की विधियों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the methods of irrigation used by the Harappans at different sites.

key_points: Trace of canals found at Shortughai
Use of water reservoirs like Dholavira

sub_questions.solution: Harappans utilized various irrigation methods. Evidence of canals has been found at the site of Shortughai in Afghanistan. It is likely that water drawn from wells was used for irrigation. Furthermore, water reservoirs found at sites like Dholavira suggest an advanced system to store rainwater for agricultural purposes.

sub_questions.text: हड़प्पा सभ्यता में लोगों के बीच सामाजिक और आर्थिक अंतरों को समझने में शवाधान किस प्रकार सहायक हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: Explain how burials help in understanding the social and economic differences amongst the people in Harappan civilization.

key_points: Jewellery and pottery in some graves

sub_questions.solution: Burials are crucial for understanding social stratification. Harappan burials often show differences in the construction of burial pits—some were lined with bricks. Furthermore, the presence of varied 'grave goods,' such as pottery, ornaments, or jewellery, indicates that some individuals were buried with more wealth than others, highlighting economic disparities.

questions.text: मौर्य साम्राज्य के बारे में जानने के विभिन्न स्रोतों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Analyse the various sources to know about the Mauryan Empire.

key_points: Literary works like Arthashastra and Indica

questions.solution: Historians use diverse sources to reconstruct the Mauryan Empire. Archaeological finds, including stone sculptures and pottery, provide physical evidence. Literary sources are vital, such as Megasthenes' 'Indica' and Kautilya's 'Arthashastra'. Additionally, Ashoka’s inscriptions on rocks and pillars are essential primary sources providing direct insights into his policies and administration.

questions.text: इब्न बतूता ने भारतीय शहरों का वर्णन किस प्रकार किया है? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain how Ibn Battuta described the Indian cities.

key_points: Cities were dense and full of opportunities

questions.solution: Ibn Battuta described Indian cities as dense, prosperous, and full of opportunities for those with drive and resources. He noted that cities were not merely centers of population but were bustling hubs of commerce, trade, and culture, with markets playing a central role in the lives of the urban inhabitants.

questions.text: मुगलों ने अपनी भू-राजस्व प्रणाली को किस प्रकार व्यवस्थित किया? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How did Mughals organize their land revenue system? Explain.
questions.solution: The Mughal land revenue system was meticulously organized. The land was classified into categories like Polaj, Parauti, etc., based on productivity. Revenue was assessed through the 'Zabt' system, and local officials like the 'patwari' and 'qanungo' maintained detailed records to ensure the state received its rightful share of the agricultural produce.

(क) समाज सुधारक के रूप में गाँधीजी की भूमिका का वर्णन कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) भारत में 1905 से 1907 के दौरान राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन की गतिविधियों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Describe the role of Gandhiji as a social reformer.
OR
(b) Explain the activities of the national movement in India during 1905 to 1907.

sub_questions.text: समाज सुधारक के रूप में गाँधीजी की भूमिका का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe the role of Gandhiji as a social reformer.

key_points: Advocated for basic education and self-reliance

sub_questions.solution: As a social reformer, Gandhiji dedicated his life to eradicating untouchability, referring to the marginalized as 'Harijans'. He tirelessly worked for Hindu-Muslim unity and promoted the spirit of self-reliance through 'Swadeshi' and rural development programs, believing that social reform was the foundation for true political independence.

sub_questions.text: भारत में 1905 से 1907 के दौरान राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन की गतिविधियों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the activities of the national movement in India during 1905 to 1907.
sub_questions.solution: The period from 1905 to 1907 was highly volatile. It began with the Partition of Bengal in 1905, which sparked the massive Swadeshi movement across the country. By 1907, the growing differences between the Moderate and Extremist factions culminated in the historic split of the Indian National Congress at the Surat session.

questions.text_english:
(a) Examine the main features of the Stupa at Sanchi and the role of the rulers of Bhopal in preserving it.
OR
(b) Examine the major teachings of Buddha and explain why Buddhism grew rapidly during the time of Buddha.

sub_questions.text: साँची के स्तूप की मुख्य विशेषताओं और इसके संरक्षण में भोपाल के शासकों की भूमिका की परख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Examine the main features of the Stupa at Sanchi and the role of the rulers of Bhopal in preserving it.

key_points: Role of Begums of Bhopal (Shahjahan Begum)

sub_questions.solution: The Sanchi Stupa is a masterpiece of Buddhist architecture, characterized by its hemispherical mound (Anda), the central Harmika, and the enclosing stone railings (Vedika) with intricately carved gateways. The rulers of Bhopal, particularly the Begums like Shahjahan Begum, played a pivotal role in its preservation. They provided essential funds for the repair and maintenance of the site, which helped prevent it from being damaged or taken to Europe, ensuring it remained as a key archaeological site in India.

sub_questions.text: बुद्ध की मुख्य शिक्षाओं की परख कीजिए और बुद्ध के समय में बौद्ध धर्म तेज़ी से क्यों बढ़ा, व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Examine the major teachings of Buddha and explain why Buddhism grew rapidly during the time of Buddha.

key_points: Four Noble Truths and Eightfold Path

sub_questions.solution: Buddha's teachings were centered on the 'Four Noble Truths' and the 'Eightfold Path' (Ashtangika Marga), which advocated for moderation and ethical living. Buddhism grew rapidly because it was accessible, emphasizing equality and rejecting the rigidity of the caste system. Furthermore, by preaching in Prakrit, the common language of the masses rather than complex Sanskrit, Buddha’s message reached everyone. His focus on non-violence (ahimsa) and personal conduct resonated with many, leading to its fast-paced spread across various social classes.

questions.text:
(क) अलवारों और नयनारों के विचारों की व्याख्या कीजिए। राज्यों के साथ इन्होंने अपने संबंध किस प्रकार स्थापित किए? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) सूफ़ीवाद के उदय के कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए और सूफ़ियों के राज्य के साथ संबंधों को भी स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Explain the ideas of Alvars and Nayanars. Elucidate how they established their relations with the states.
OR
(b) Explain the causes of the growth of Sufism and also explain the Sufis relations with the state.

sub_questions.text: अलवारों और नयनारों के विचारों की व्याख्या कीजिए। राज्यों के साथ इन्होंने अपने संबंध किस प्रकार स्थापित किए?
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the ideas of Alvars and Nayanars. Elucidate how they established their relations with the states.

key_points: Inclusion of their hymns in temples

sub_questions.solution: Alvars (devotees of Vishnu) and Nayanars (devotees of Shiva) were Tamil saint-poets who promoted 'Bhakti'—personal devotion to God. Their movement rejected caste-based inequalities and emphasized that the divine was accessible to everyone. They established deep relations with states; for instance, the Chola rulers patronized them by building grand temples and incorporating their hymns into rituals. This royal patronage elevated the Bhakti movement, making it an integral part of the state's cultural and religious fabric.

sub_questions.text: सूफ़ीवाद के उदय के कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए और सूफ़ियों के राज्य के साथ संबंधों को भी स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the causes of the growth of Sufism and also explain the Sufis relations with the state.

key_points: Relations with rulers (varying from distance to proximity)

sub_questions.solution: Sufism grew as a reaction against the rigid orthodoxy and formalism of institutional Islam, seeking a personal and mystical connection with God. Sufi 'Khanqahs' became centers of spiritual learning. Their relationship with the state varied; while some Sufis kept a distance from royal power, others were closely linked to rulers. Rulers often sought their blessings, while Sufis accepted land grants (inams) and occasionally influenced state policy, balancing their spiritual autonomy with the realities of political power.

questions.text:
(क) बंगाल में इस्तमरारी बंदोबस्त के कार्यान्वयन और इसके परिणामों को प्रभावित करने वाले कारकों की परख कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) “18वीं शताब्दी के अंत में उत्तर बंगाल के कुछ क्षेत्रों में जोतदार प्रभावशाली बन गए थे।” इस कथन की परख कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Examine the factors that influenced the implementation of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal and its consequences.
OR
(b) “The jotedars became powerful figures in many areas of North Bengal during the end of the 18th century.” Examine the statement.

sub_questions.text: बंगाल में इस्तमरारी बंदोबस्त के कार्यान्वयन और इसके परिणामों को प्रभावित करने वाले कारकों की परख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Examine the factors that influenced the implementation of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal and its consequences.

key_points: Creation of a loyal landlord class

sub_questions.solution: The Permanent Settlement (1793) aimed to ensure a stable revenue income for the East India Company and create a class of loyal landlords. However, the high revenue demands often led to the auctioning of estates when zamindars failed to pay on time. This caused the displacement of traditional zamindars and empowered new purchasers—rich urban merchants and moneylenders—who often had little interest in agricultural improvement but were skilled at extracting maximum rent from the peasants.

sub_questions.text: “18वीं शताब्दी के अंत में उत्तर बंगाल के कुछ क्षेत्रों में जोतदार प्रभावशाली बन गए थे।” इस कथन की परख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: “The jotedars became powerful figures in many areas of North Bengal during the end of the 18th century.” Examine the statement.

key_points: Control over local trade and credit

sub_questions.solution: Jotedars were rich peasants who emerged as a powerful social class in North Bengal. They controlled vast tracts of land and dominated local trade and credit, often becoming more powerful than the traditional zamindars in their villages. They resisted the zamindar's attempts to increase rent, extended loans to poor peasants, and exercised direct influence over the rural population. Their rise shifted the power balance in the countryside, as they effectively functioned as the real masters of the local economy, challenging the zamindari structure.

हौज़ों/जलाशयों का निर्माण किस प्रकार होता था?
कृष्णदेव राय द्वारा बनवाए गए जलाशय के विषय में पेस लिखता है:
राजा ने एक जलाशय बनवाया दो पहाड़ियों के मुख-विबर पर जिससे दोनों में से किसी पहाड़ी से आने वाला सारा जल वहाँ इकट्ठा हो, इसके अलावा जल 9 मील (लगभग 15 किमी) से भी अधिक की दूरी से पाइपों से आता है जो बाहरी श्रृंखला के निचले हिस्से के साथ-साथ बनाए गए थे। यह जल एक झील से लाया जाता है जो छलकाव से खुद एक छोटी नदी में मिलती है। जलाशय में तीन विशाल स्तंभ बने हैं जिन पर खूबसूरती से चित्र उकेरे गए हैं; ये ऊपरी भाग में कुछ पाइपों से जुड़े हुए हैं जिनसे ये अपने बगीचों तथा धान के खेतों की सिंचाई के लिए पानी लाते हैं। इस जलाशय को बनाने के लिए इस राजा ने एक पूरी पहाड़ी को तुड़वा दिया... जलाशय में मैंने इतने लोगों को कार्य करते देखा कि वहाँ पन्द्रह से बीस हज़ार आदमी थे, चींटियों की तरह...
(32.1) कृष्णदेव राय ने जलाशय का निर्माण क्यों करवाया?
(32.2) कृष्णदेव राय ने जलाशय के निर्माण के लिए दो पहाड़ियों के मुख-विबर के स्थान को क्यों चुना?
(32.3) जलाशयों के पानी का उपयोग किस प्रकार किया जाता था?
questions.text_english:
How tanks were built?
About a tank constructed by Krishnadeva Raya, Paes wrote:
The king made a tank at the mouth of two hills so that all the water which comes from either one side or the other collects there; and, besides this, water comes to it from more than three leagues (approximately 15 kilometres) by pipes which run along the lower parts of the range outside. This water is brought from a lake which itself overflows into a little river. The tank has three large pillars handsomely carved with figures; these connect above with certain pipes by which they get water when they have to irrigate their gardens and rice-fields. In order to make this tank the said king broke down a hill ... In the tank I saw so many people at work that there must have been fifteen or twenty thousand men, looking like ants
(32.1) Why did Krishnadeva Raya construct a tank?
(32.2) Why did Krishnadeva Raya choose the location at the mouth of two hills for building the tank?
(32.3) In what ways was the water from the tanks used?

sub_questions.text: कृष्णदेव राय ने जलाशय का निर्माण क्यों करवाया?
sub_questions.text_english: Why did Krishnadeva Raya construct a tank?

key_points: To store water for agricultural use
To ensure reliable irrigation for gardens and rice fields

sub_questions.solution: Krishnadeva Raya constructed the tank primarily to ensure a reliable source of water for the irrigation of gardens and rice fields, supporting the kingdom's agricultural economy.

sub_questions.text: कृष्णदेव राय ने जलाशय के निर्माण के लिए दो पहाड़ियों के मुख-विबर के स्थान को क्यों चुना?
sub_questions.text_english: Why did Krishnadeva Raya choose the location at the mouth of two hills for building the tank?

key_points: To collect water flowing from both hills
Strategic terrain for maximum water accumulation

sub_questions.solution: He chose the mouth of two hills so that all the runoff water from both hills could be efficiently captured and collected in a single central location.

sub_questions.text: जलाशयों के पानी का उपयोग किस प्रकार किया जाता था?
sub_questions.text_english: In what ways was the water from the tanks used?

key_points: Connected via pipes to supply fields

sub_questions.solution: The water collected in the tank was directed through specially constructed pipes connected to the structure. These pipes supplied necessary water for irrigating the royal gardens and agricultural rice fields.

questions.text:
नवाब साहब जा चुके हैं
एक और गीत में ऐसे शासक की दुर्दशा पर विलाप किया जा रहा है जिसे मजबूरन अपनी मातृभूमि छोड़नी पड़ी:
अभिजात और किसान, सब रो रहे थे। और सारा आलम रोता-चिल्लाता था। हाय! जान-ए-आलम देस से विदा लेकर परदेस चले गए हैं।
(33.1) नवाब को हटाने का तत्काल प्रभाव क्या पड़ा?
(33.2) नवाब के गद्दी से हटने और जाने पर भावनात्मक उथल-पुथल क्यों मची?
(33.3) अवध का अधिग्रहण अंग्रेज़ों की औपनिवेशिक रणनीति में किस प्रकार सही रहा? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
The Nawab has left
Another song mourned the plight of the ruler who had to leave his motherland:
Noble and peasant all wept together and all the world wept and wailed. Alas! The chief has bidden adieu to his country and gone abroad.
(33.1) What was the immediate impact of the removal of the Nawab?
(33.2) Why was there emotional upheaval at the dethroning and departure of the Nawab?
(33.3) How did the annexation of Awadh fit into the British colonial strategy? Explain.

sub_questions.text: नवाब को हटाने का तत्काल प्रभाव क्या पड़ा?
sub_questions.text_english: What was the immediate impact of the removal of the Nawab?

key_points: Widespread mourning among nobles and peasants
Sense of loss throughout the realm

sub_questions.solution: The immediate impact was widespread grief; nobles and peasants alike wept, and there was a profound sense of loss and sorrow across the entire kingdom upon the Nawab's departure.

sub_questions.text: नवाब के गद्दी से हटने और जाने पर भावनात्मक उथल-पुथल क्यों मची?
sub_questions.text_english: Why was there emotional upheaval at the dethroning and departure of the Nawab?

key_points: Symbolic connection between ruler and subjects

sub_questions.solution: The emotional upheaval occurred because the Nawab was seen as a symbol of the land. His forced departure represented not just a change in ruler, but the loss of a protector and a deep severance from their motherland, causing collective despair.

sub_questions.text: अवध का अधिग्रहण अंग्रेज़ों की औपनिवेशिक रणनीति में किस प्रकार सही रहा?
sub_questions.text_english: How did the annexation of Awadh fit into the British colonial strategy? Explain.

key_points: To complete the process of expanding British control
Strategic control of a fertile and wealthy region
Justified by accusing the Nawab of misgovernance

sub_questions.solution: The annexation of Awadh (1856) was a key move in British colonial strategy to expand and consolidate their control over North India. By accusing the Nawab of misgovernance, the British justified their takeover of a fertile and prosperous region, ensuring total administrative and economic control over a territory that had been a long-standing ally, ultimately finalizing the expansionist agenda.
